messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (P1) — service: inference-serving, symptom: high 5xx rate, region: us-west-az6, alert-rule: nic-errors > 50/min. Pager: oncall@redwood
pd-bot: PagerDuty incident INC3950012345 created and routed to oncall rota: oncall-rotation. Escalation policy applied.
Lucy Torres: Acked on PD, I'm taking this. Looking at zonal metrics now. :eyes:
SRE Ops: seeing interface flaps on several GPU hosts in az6, kernel logs show repeated link state changes. A few model shards lost connectivity -> 502s and connection resets.
SRE Ops: quick grep from node-123: ```Mar 15 12:05:33 kernel: e1000e 0000:af:00.1: NIC Link is Down``` several similar lines across hosts
Raj Patel: Any signs of DDoS or traffic surge? Our external metrics for requests/sec are steady for the region, looks like infra-level NIC flaps.
Lucy Torres: Confirmed. Error budget for az6 route spiking. Starting traffic diversion to az5 (gradual). Posting runbook steps now.
Maria Chen: Customer impact? Which tenants are hit? Need to notify CS and update status page if >10% of requests failing.
SRE Ops: Preliminary tenant mapping shows a handful of high-throughput customers with traffic routed through az6 - estimate 12% of total gen requests failing. Will refine in 10m.
Lucy Torres: Executing controlled divert: ```/controlplane route modify --region us-west --from az6 --to az5 --percent 30 --comment "auto-divert nic flap"``` will ramp over 5 min.
Dan O'Neill: If we push 30% now, watch tail latency in az5. If az5 saturates, fallback to universal fallback pool (dedicated-fallback-1).
SRE Ops: Reducing batch size on az6 nodes to reduce retry storms: ```reconf batching --cluster az6 --max-batch-tokens 512``` also disabling non-critical background jobs on affected nodes.
incident-bot: Automatic action: route-divert started (30% -> az5). Will auto-increase to 70% if 5xx rate doesn't drop by 50% in 10m.
Lucy Torres: PD escalation to SRE lead @Dan O'Neill (ack escalated). Dan can you join bridge?
Dan O'Neill: Joining bridge. Oncall handoff in 10m if stable. I'll take ownership until resolved.
SRE Ops: Observed kernel-level parity errors on NIC firmware for vendor X. Logged firmware version mismatch on 6 hosts. Neteng looped in.
Raj Patel: Neteng advised to isolate the top offending hosts from LB and trigger NIC reset: ```ssh node-123 sudo ethtool -r eth0``` doing one at a time.
Lucy Torres: Doing host isolation now. Marking 4 hosts out of rotation. Early lift in 5xx to 8% from 12% after removing two hosts.
Maria Chen: Can we limit model fallbacks to preserve quality? Prefer to keep model variant locked for enterprise tenants — set routing filters.
SRE Ops: Applied tenant routing: enterprise customers pinned to az5 fallback path only; public traffic gets diverted evenly. Command: ```/controlplane tenant route set --tenant enterprise --route az5```
pd-bot: PagerDuty: escalation sent to SRE Lead & NetEng. Reminder: incident priority remains P1 until degraded rate <1% for 30m.
Lucy Torres: Quick customer note draft: "We are investigating an infrastructure-level networking issue in us-west-az6 causing increased errors for some generation requests. We are diverting traffic and mitigating the impact. No action required from customers; updates every 15 minutes." Anyone want to edit?
Maria Chen: Add ETA we expect substantial recovery in 30-45m unless firmware roll needed.
Lucy Torres: Updated and posted to status page.
SRE Ops: Running health check on KV cache shards. Some cache thrashing observed due to retries. Kicking off warm-reload on kvcache nodes to rehydrate prefixes.
Dan O'Neill: If diverting triggers overload in az5, automatically drop lower-priority routes (reranking, heavy-batch jobs). Please pre-stage policy: ```route policy set --priority low --action drop-on-overload```
incident-bot: Alert: route-divert ramp to 70% scheduled (auto) if 5xx persists. Monitoring window 10m.
Lucy Torres: Handing on-call to Dan O'Neill in 10m. I'll remain on-thread for customer comms. :handshake:
oncall-rotation: Handed off to Dan O'Neill at 3950012450.
Dan O'Neill: Taking over. Current metrics: az6 5xx 7.8%, az5 1.1%, overall error impact ~6%. Continuing host isolates, coordinating firmware rollback with NetEng.
SRE Ops: NetEng recommends rolling NIC firmware on isolated hosts; prep script ready: ```./fw-roll.sh --hosts host1,host2 --rollback-to 1.2.3```. Will stagger roll to avoid capacity shock.
Raj Patel: I'll run the first staged roll on host1 and monitor traffic. Ping when you want me to proceed.
Dan O'Neill: Proceed. After first host roll, monitor 5xx and CPU on az5. If stable, continue in batches of 2.
SRE Ops: First batch completed, host1/host2 rolled back. Link stability improved on those nodes, 5xx partial reduction observed.
Lucy Torres: Notifying CS: posted update to customers list, support teams cc'd. Asking CS to open targeted incident tickets for top-affected tenants.
Maria Chen: Good. Also advise product to temporarily suspend high-contrast eval runs that could amplify load.
Raj Patel: Running smoke tests across the cluster: samples OK from az5 fallback. Latency slightly higher (~80ms p95) but acceptable.
pd-bot: PagerDuty note: incident updated by Lucy Torres — action: traffic divert + host isolation + firmware rollback started. Next escalation in 30m if not resolved.
Dan O'Neill: Planning to keep incident active until az6 5xx < 1% for 30 minutes. Tentative ETA 45-60m depending on firmware progress.
SRE Ops: Rolling remaining hosts in staggered batches now. Keep an eye on autoscaler to avoid spinning up extra nodes in az5.
Lucy Torres: Thanks team. I'll keep customer-facing updates every 15m. Dan takeover confirmed. Closing loop with exec if >1h.
Dan O'Neill: Acknowledged. Continuing ops. I'll post another status at 3950012540."
